summary: Some widows were allowed to their husbands but are forbidden to the brother who would do yibum, because of who he is. The mishnah gives examples, like a widow whose brother-in-law is the Kohen Gadol.

chunks.en: Some women are allowed to their husbands but forbidden to their yevamin,

chunks.en: These are allowed to their husbands but forbidden to their yevamin:
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: And these are cases of women who are permitted to their husbands and forbidden to their yevamin:

chunks.en: A regular Kohen who married a widow
chunks.st: In the case of a common priest who married a widow,

chunks.en: and has a brother who is Kohen Gadol,
chunks.st: and he has a brother who is the High Priest, the widow, who was permitted to her husband, is forbidden to her yavam, as it is prohibited for the High Priest to marry a widow.

chunks.en: a chalal who married a woman fit for a Kohen
chunks.st: The same is true in the case of a priest disqualified due to flawed lineage [ḥalal], e.g., the son of a priest and a divorcée, who married a woman fit to marry a priest,

words.note: A son of a Kohen born from a marriage forbidden to Kohanim; he is not a full Kohen.

chunks.en: and has a brother who is a fit Kohen,
chunks.st: and he has a brother who is a priest fit for service.
chunks.stMore: That woman was permitted to marry the ḥalal but is forbidden to his brother. Having engaged in intercourse with the ḥalal, she is rendered a ḥalala, a woman disqualified from marrying a priest.

chunks.en: a regular Jew who married a Jewish woman
chunks.st: Another example is the case of an Israelite of unflawed lineage who married an Israelite woman of similar lineage,

chunks.en: and has a brother who is a mamzer,
chunks.st: and he has a brother who is a son born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship [mamzer];

chunks.en: a mamzer who married a mamzeres
chunks.st: or a mamzer who married a daughter born from an incestuous or adulterous relationship [mamzeret],

chunks.en: and has a brother who is a regular Jew:
chunks.st: and he has a brother who is an Israelite of unflawed lineage. A mamzer is permitted to marry a mamzeret, but neither is per-mitted to a Jew of unflawed lineage.

chunks.en: these are allowed to their husbands but forbidden to their yevamin.
chunks.st: In each of these cases, these women are permitted to their husbands and forbidden to their yevamin.

summary: Other women are forbidden to their husbands but allowed to the yavam, and some are forbidden to both. All other women are allowed to both.

summary: Relatives forbidden only by the Rabbis (sheniyos) may be forbidden to the husband, to the yavam, or to both. A woman in such a marriage gets no kesubah, but women in some marriages forbidden by the Torah do get one.

chunks.en: one who is a sheniyah to the husband but not to the yavam
chunks.st: a secondary relative to the husband but not a secondary relative to the yavam, she

chunks.en: She gets no kesubah,
chunks.st: she does not have the right to receive payment for her marriage contract if divorced or widowed,

chunks.en: no payment for the fruits of her property,
chunks.st: nor is she entitled to payment from her husband for the produce of her property that he used,

chunks.en: no food,
chunks.st: nor is she entitled to provisions for her sustenance from his estate,

chunks.en: and no worn-out clothes.
chunks.explain: She does not get back the old things she brought into the marriage.
chunks.st: nor does she get back her worn clothes or other objects she brought with her to her marriage.
